Model Workspace and Data Management

Source: vignettes/model_workspace.Rmd
model_workspace.Rmd
library(multimod)

Overview

The multimod package provides a flexible workspace system for managing models and their data on disk. This vignette demonstrates:

  • Creating and managing model workspaces
  • Saving and loading models in different formats
  • Working with in-memory vs on-disk data
  • Updating parameters and mappings
  • Lazy loading for large models
  • Cross-language data interoperability

Storage Architecture

Hybrid Approach

The storage system uses a hybrid approach that balances R-specific needs with cross-language compatibility:

  • model.rds: Complete R model object (structure, metadata, equations, variables, ASTs)
  • Data files: Stored separately in cross-language formats (Arrow IPC, CSV, Parquet)
  • metadata.json: Human-readable summary for non-R users

This design allows: - Fast loading of R model structure (single RDS file) - Cross-language access to data (Python, Julia can read Arrow/CSV) - Atomic updates (one model.rds contains all structure)

Directory Structure 

model_path/
  model.rds              # Complete R model object with all structure
  metadata.json          # Human-readable summary
  format.txt             # Data format: "csv", "ipc", or "parquet"
  solution_log.txt       # Log of solution loads (appended on each load)
  sets/
    set_name.txt         # Set members (one per line)
  parameters/
    param_name/
      data.{csv|arrow|parquet}      # Parameter data only
      folded_data/
        data.{csv|arrow|parquet}    # Folded data if exists
  mappings/
    mapping_name/
      data.{csv|arrow|parquet}      # Mapping data only
  variables/             # Solution values (moved from solver on load_results)
    var_name/
      data.{csv|arrow|parquet}      # Variable solution values
  solvers/
    jump/                # JuMP (Julia) solver files
      model.jl           # Generated Julia/JuMP code
      data.jl            # Data loading functions
      solution/          # Latest solve results (overwritten each run)
        var_name/
          data.{csv|arrow|parquet}  # Variable solution values
    gmpl/                # GMPL (GLPK) solver files
      model.mod          # Generated GMPL code

Storage Formats

CSV (Universal) 

# Default format - human-readable, works everywhere
model <- save_model(
  model,
  path = "models/my_model",
  format = "csv"
)

Pros: - Universal compatibility - Human-readable - Easy debugging

Cons: - Largest file size - Slower I/O

IPC/Arrow (Recommended) 

# Recommended format - fast and compact
model <- save_model(
  model,
  path = "models/my_model",
  format = "ipc",
  compression = "zstd",
  compression_level = 15
)

Pros: - Fast I/O (10-20x faster than CSV) - Good compression (2-3x smaller than CSV) - Cross-language (Python, Julia, R) - Column-oriented (efficient queries)

Cons: - Binary format (not human-readable) - Requires Arrow library

Parquet (Compact) 

# Most compact but slower
model <- save_model(
  model,
  path = "models/my_model",
  format = "parquet",
  compression = "zstd",
  compression_level = 15
)

Pros: - Best compression (3-4x smaller than CSV) - Wide ecosystem support

Cons: - Slower than IPC - More complex format

Basic Workflow

1. Save a Model 

library(multimod)

# Load or create a model
data(example_models)
demo_model <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
model <- demo_model

# Save with default settings (CSV format)
model <- save_model(
  model,
  path = "models/utopia",
  verbose = TRUE
)

2. Load a Model 

# Load complete model with all data
model <- load_model(
  path = "models/utopia",
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Access parameters
tech_cost <- model$parameters$pTechCost$data
demand <- model$parameters$pDemand$data

3. Update Parameters 

# Modify parameter data
new_demand <- demand
new_demand$value <- new_demand$value * 1.1  # 10% increase

# Update in model
model <- update_parameter(
  model,
  name = "pDemand",
  data = new_demand
)

# Save changes
model <- save_model(model, path = "models/utopia", overwrite = TRUE)

Advanced Features

Lazy Loading

For large models, load structure without data:

# Load only model structure (no data in memory)
model <- load_model(
  path = "models/utopia",
  load_data = FALSE
)

# Model structure is available
print(names(model$parameters))
print(model$parameters$pDemand$sets)

# Load specific parameters on demand
demand_data <- get_data(model, "pDemand", type = "parameter")

# get_data() automatically loads from disk and caches in model
# Subsequent calls use the cached data
demand_data2 <- get_data(model, "pDemand", type = "parameter")  # From cache

Auto-Save on Update 

# Load model from disk
model <- load_model("models/utopia")

# Update parameter with immediate save to disk
model <- update_parameter(
  model,
  name = "pDemand",
  data = new_demand_data,
  auto_save = TRUE  # Writes immediately to disk
)

# No need for separate save_model() call

Memory Management 

# Save model and free data from memory
model <- save_model(
  model,
  path = "models/utopia",
  keep_in_memory = FALSE  # Removes data from model object
)

# Model structure remains, but data is NULL
is.null(model$parameters$pDemand$data)  # TRUE

# Use get_data() to load from disk when needed
demand <- get_data(model, "pDemand", type = "parameter")

Solution Management

The package provides integrated solution storage for solver results:

# Solve model and load results
result <- solve_jump(
  model = demo_model,
  model_dir = "models/utopia",
  load_results = TRUE
)

# Update model with loaded solutions
model <- result$model

# Solutions are now in model$variables[[var_name]]$solution
vObjective <- model$variables$vObjective$solution
vTechCap <- model$variables$vTechCap$solution

# Solution metadata
print(model$solution_metadata$loaded_at)
print(model$solution_metadata$variables_loaded)

# Check solution log
log <- readLines("models/utopia/solution_log.txt")
print(tail(log, 5))

Solution Storage Workflow:

  1. Solver writes: Solutions saved to solvers/jump/solution/ (overwrites previous)
  2. Load results: If load_results=TRUE, solutions copied to variables/ (overwrites previous)
  3. Log append: Each load appends timestamp and variable list to solution_log.txt

Benefits: - Simple structure: one current solution in solver directory - Audit trail: log tracks all solution loads with timestamps - Clean workspace: no proliferation of timestamped directories - Overwrite behavior: easy to re-run and update solutions


## Working with Folded Data

Models with folded parameters store both regular and folded data:


``` r
# Apply folding
model <- fold_parameter(model, "pDemand", dimensions = "slice")

# Save model - both data and folded_data are saved
model <- save_model(model, path = "models/utopia_folded", format = "ipc")

# Load and access folded data
model <- load_model("models/utopia_folded")
demand_regular <- model$parameters$pDemand$data
demand_folded <- model$parameters$pDemand$folded_data$data

# Update with folded data
model <- update_parameter(
  model,
  name = "pDemand",
  data = new_regular_data,
  folded_data = new_folded_data
)

Cross-Language Interoperability

From R 

# Save in Arrow IPC format
save_model(model, "models/shared", format = "ipc")

From Python 

import pyarrow.feather as feather
import pandas as pd

# Read parameter data
demand = feather.read_feather("models/shared/parameters/pDemand/data.arrow")
print(demand.head())

# Read set members
with open("models/shared/sets/region.txt", "r") as f:
    regions = [line.strip() for line in f]

From Julia 

using Arrow

# Read parameter data
demand = Arrow.Table("models/shared/parameters/pDemand/data.arrow")
df = DataFrame(demand)

Complete Example 

library(multimod)

# 1. Create or load model
data(example_models)
demo_model <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
model <- demo_model

# 2. Modify some parameters
demand <- model$parameters$pDemand$data
demand$value <- demand$value * 1.05  # 5% increase

model <- update_parameter(model, "pDemand", demand)

# 3. Save with recommended format
model <- save_model(
  model,
  path = "models/utopia_scenario1",
  format = "ipc",
  compression = "zstd",
  compression_level = 15,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# 4. Generate and solve with JuMP
write_jump(model, model_dir = "models/utopia_scenario1")

result <- solve_jump(
  model = model,
  model_dir = "models/utopia_scenario1",
  method = "system",
  load_results = TRUE
)

# Update model with solutions
model <- result$model

# 5. Access solution values
vObjective <- model$variables$vObjective$solution
vTechCap <- model$variables$vTechCap$solution

print(paste("Objective value:", vObjective$value))
print(head(vTechCap))

# 6. Check solution log
solution_log <- readLines("models/utopia_scenario1/solution_log.txt")
cat(tail(solution_log, 3), sep = "\n")

# 7. For large models: lazy loading
model_structure <- load_model(
  "models/utopia_scenario1",
  load_data = FALSE
)

# Load only needed parameters
demand <- get_data(model_structure, "pDemand", type = "parameter")
tech_cost <- get_data(model_structure, "pTechCost", type = "parameter")

Performance Comparison

Approximate performance for a typical model:

Format Size Save Time Load Time Compression
CSV 1.2 MB 100% 100% 1.0x
IPC 0.6 MB 15% 10% 2.0x
Parquet 0.3 MB 40% 30% 3.6x

Recommendation: Use IPC format for best balance of speed, size, and compatibility.

Best Practices

  1. Use IPC format for production models (fast, compact, cross-language)
  2. Use lazy loading for large models to minimize memory usage
  3. Use auto_save when making incremental updates to on-disk models
  4. Keep model.rds together with data files (don’t separate them)
  5. Use version control for model.rds (it’s deterministic for same model state)
  6. Document changes in metadata.json (edit manually if needed)
  7. Check solution_log.txt to track when solutions were loaded and updated
  8. Use load_results=TRUE to automatically move solutions from solver to model root

Workflow Summary

Import/Create → Update → Save → Generate → Solve → Access Solutions

Troubleshooting

Large Models 

# Use lazy loading
model <- load_model("models/large_model", load_data = FALSE)

# Process parameters one at a time
for (param_name in names(model$parameters)) {
  data <- get_data(model, param_name, type = "parameter")
  # ... process data ...
  # Clear from memory if needed
  model$parameters[[param_name]]$data <- NULL
}

Disk Space 

# Use Parquet for maximum compression
save_model(model, "models/compact", format = "parquet")

# Or remove data from memory after saving
model <- save_model(model, "models/compact", keep_in_memory = FALSE)

Corrupted Files 

# Model structure is separate from data
# If data file corrupted, structure is still in model.rds

model <- readRDS("models/my_model/model.rds")

# Re-import or regenerate the corrupted parameter
model <- update_parameter(model, "pDemand", new_data, auto_save = TRUE)
